findings.where: the bottom third from frame 002 to the end; final frame rectangles at (50,1232) 721x511 px and (50,1781) 721x235 px
findings.what: Notes are drawn as flat cream rectangles: fill ratio 1.0000, top and bottom edge straightness std 0.00 px, all four corners square-filled, no tear, no contact shadow (wood 3 px below the lower rectangle reads 93.5 against 96.9 at 40-60 px below, a 3.4-level difference), and interior micro-texture of 0.95 high-pass sigma-1.5 std against 6.23 for the real 'empty chair' note stock in the same frame; 25 of 26 sampled frames contain one, up to 21.3 per cent of the frame.
findings.why: A flat beige rectangle standing in for paper is the rubric row's own below-floor condition and the fourth anti-goal, and here it is the largest single surface in most of the clip.

findings.what: The clip contains no unfolding: mean absolute inter-frame change is 1.28 of 255 (0.005, matching frames.json mean_change_per_frame 0.0058), the only large step is the frame 1 to 2 scene cut at 38.0, and the change between frames 2 and 6 covers a 914x1944 px bounding box, i.e. the whole page translating, not a local crease; stepping frames 1, 11, 21 ... 253 shows a chat list scrolling and nothing folding.
findings.why: The rubric row is judged 'in slow motion on the unfolding clip' for Blender-rendered folds and creases under one consistent light direction; no fold exists anywhere in the five clips, so that half of the row is entirely undemonstrated. surfaces.json asserts a 240-frame 'unfold_thirds' sequence exists as an asset, which makes its absence from the capture an omission rather than a reason.

findings.where: the desk between the notes, e.g. the bands at y 1589-1601, y 2032-2036, y 2545 and y 437/2568
findings.what: The desk carries a tiled repeating scratch texture. Bright hairlines sit on constant scanlines at exact pitches: four at 67 px pitch (y1589-1601, widths 24-31 px), four at 103-106 px pitch (y2032-2036, widths 37-44 px), four at 104-105 px pitch (y2545, widths 39-49 px), four at 64-65 px pitch (y313-317, widths 25-28 px), and four at 253-277 px pitch (y437 and y2568, widths 91-124 px) - constant length, constant y, constant spacing, several repeats inside one screen.
findings.why: A tiled repeating texture visible on a single screen is named in the rubric row as a below-floor condition, and the desk is the surface every note sits on (48.9 per cent of this frame).

findings.where: the note at y 1630-1830, 'The folder is open. It has been / open on the table for nine / days.'
findings.what: Repeated letters are the same outline. The 'e' at (377,1682) and the 'e' at (371,1766) have ink-mask IoU 0.9954 (434 vs 432 ink px, mean absolute grey difference 2.1); the 'e' at (1064,1755) and (796,1759) IoU 0.9644; the 'l' stems at (494,1662) and (777,1742) IoU 0.9426. Across the four 'e's on that note there are exactly two distinct outlines, each used twice.
findings.why: The row requires handwriting with multiple variants per glyph; the build's own evidence/logs/hand.json agrees and fails itself - 145 of 484 marks have a near-twin at IoU 0.85, twin_share 0.30, best_fit_iou max 1.0, "ok": false.

findings.where: the ink of the same note, y 1630-1830, x 200-1280
findings.what: There is no pressure variance. Eroded ink-core pixels take only three discrete values before antialiasing (53, 58, 62) and 67.4 per cent of them are exactly grey 58; the two 'l' stems measure 6 to 8 px wide over 43 and 42 sampled rows (mean 7.2 px, std 0.7). No thick-to-thin modulation, no ink pooling at terminals or joins, no density change anywhere along a stroke.
findings.why: The row requires 'real pressure variance'; a flat single-value fill inside a constant-width outline with a 1 px edge jitter is a font with roughened contours, not a pen.

findings.what: The object's shadow is an unblurred near-black quadrilateral, not a contact shadow: 564 pixels below grey level 55 surround the card and appear on every side at once - 160 above and 404 below its centroid (y 1319), 307 left and 257 right of it (x 1312) - with a vertical scan at x=1380 stepping wood 77 to black 21 to card 184 across 2 px, a maximum gradient of 122 grey levels per pixel.
findings.why: The row asks for contact shadows baked from the render's own lighting; a hard black quad visible on opposite sides of one object cannot come from any single light, and it is not even a uniform blur.

findings.where: frame 250, the candle's cast shadow on the note, scan line y 618-622
findings.what: The shadow core is a plateau of constant opacity: across x 490-670 the value is 128 +/- 2 with no gradient at all over 180 px, then ramps to the unshadowed paper value of 229 only in the outermost ~40 px. The candle body itself carries almost no material: high-pass sigma-1.5 std 1.14 against 3.10 for the paper it sits on.
findings.why: A flat-cored blob with a single soft rim is a uniform blur, which the row explicitly contrasts against a shadow baked from the render's lighting; a real penumbra darkens toward contact and lightens with distance.

findings.where: the final frame (395), the 'hold' note at x 100-960, y 260-500
findings.what: A large soft grey shadow disc lies across the note with nothing casting it - the candle that would cast it is not present anywhere in the frame - and the disc is cut flat by the note's own top boundary rather than by any geometry.
findings.why: A shadow that survives its object is an applied decoration, not lighting; the row's whole point is that shadows come from the render.

findings.where: the desk everywhere, and the drawn knot at x 640-780, y 1520-1620
findings.what: The desk, 48.9 per cent of the Chat hero, is drawn rather than photographed: high-pass sigma-1.5 std 4.97 against 13.33 for the note stock in the same frame, R/G channel-ratio std 0.038 over a 150x1240 px patch (one hue modulated only in lightness), and a 'knot' made of evenly spaced concentric ellipses through which the vertical grain bands run undeflected. In all five clips it degrades further into flat vector woodgrain - see 06_unfolding.mp4 frame 256 at x 770, where the drawn grain meets the paper along a mathematically straight vertical line.
findings.why: The row asks for material that reads as photographed; the surface that everything else rests on is the most visible material in the app and it reads as an illustration at 300 per cent.

findings.where: the top and bottom of the list through the middle of the clip
findings.what: 14 of 31 sampled frames also carry a flat, mathematically rectangular, untextured cream panel (fill ratio >= 0.995, top-edge std < 0.5 px, interior high-pass std < 2.0), the largest 4.8 per cent of the frame.
findings.why: Same failure as 06, at smaller scale: paper standing in as an untextured rectangle.

findings.where: the final frame (395), bottom note, x 604-779, y 1925-2010
findings.what: 110 adjacent columns are perfectly constant down 85 rows (per-column vertical std < 1.5 while the horizontal spread of those column means is 40.6) - a band of single-grey vertical bars where the 'a squeeze' object's render is smeared, and the note and its shadow are cut off by a straight horizontal edge below it.
findings.why: A visible raster smear across a rendered object contradicts the claim that these objects are rendered geometry catching light.

findings.what: The log states floor_units 26.0 but reports min 18.8 for NoorHand.ttf and 11.7 for TeoHand.ttf, then lists "too_close": [] and "ok": true for both.
findings.why: A measurement whose own minimum sits below its own stated floor while reporting no offenders cannot be used to support the claim that glyph variants are far enough apart; the pixels on the hero show why it should not be trusted.

what_is_working: The note stock itself reads as scanned at 300 per cent: the crop evidence/crops/02_chat_300_hand.png shows fibre grain and a fibrous, non-uniform tear fringe, and the paper measures 13.33 high-pass sigma-1.5 std against 4.97 for the desk in the same frame; surfaces.json lists 54 paper surfaces, the lowest at patch_std 2.288 against a 1.2 floor.

Tear masks do not repeat on a single screen. Taking the high-frequency component of all twelve top and bottom paper contours in 02_chat.png, the largest pairwise cross-correlation is 0.512 (between the top and bottom of the same note) and the largest between two different notes is 0.454 - independently confirming evidence/logs/tears.json (8 visible, 8 distinct, pool 56, no repeats).

Light direction on the notes is single and consistent. Binning the wood around each of the six notes in 02_chat.png by the direction of its nearest paper pixel, all six are darkest where the paper lies to the pixel's left (55, 57, 60, 63, 65, 71) and brightest on the opposite side (90 to 105) - one light from the upper left, agreeing across every note and with the candle's down-right cast shadow in 07_feeling_landing.mp4.

Feelings are physical objects, not icons: the confetti spheres, the 'hold' candle, the 'nyeh' ribbon and the creased 'a squeeze' sheet are rendered geometry with specular highlights, and the spheres' highlight directions agree to within a 14 degree standard deviation (mean 209 degrees, upper-left).

11_chat_scroll.mp4 carries genuine material variety across one scroll - yellow legal, index card, graph, lined and receipt stocks, a folded-corner card, and a real photograph inside a note - with no flat untextured rectangle in any sampled frame.
verdict: The paper itself is real and the tears are real - at 300 per cent the note stock shows fibre and the twelve tear contours on the Chat hero correlate no higher than 0.51 with each other - and the six notes agree on one light from the upper left. Everything else the row asks for is either missing or simulated. The clip named for unfolding contains no unfolding at all (mean inter-frame change 0.005, one scene cut, a page translating), so the Blender-rendered folds and creases the row is meant to be judged on cannot be judged; in that same clip 25 of 26 sampled frames put a flat cream rectangle in place of a note - fill ratio 1.0000, edge straightness 0.00 px, six times less micro-texture than the real stock beside it, no contact shadow - which is the row's own below-floor condition and the fourth anti-goal, and the desk under everything carries scratch hairlines repeating at exact 67 px, 105 px and 265 px pitches within one screen, which is the other. The handwriting fails both of its clauses at once: repeated 'e's on one note match at IoU 0.995 and the ink is a flat fill with 67 per cent of its core pixels at exactly grey 58. Two of the three shadows I could measure are not lighting - the 'goodnight' card's is an unblurred black quad appearing on all four sides simultaneously, and the candle's is a plateau flat to within two grey levels across 180 px. The category is below its floor on three separate blocking grounds; I score it 13 of 25.
